I am in. I had a decent year, but some things didn't work as well as expected. Most of these were in a long raised bed, planted in a rather loose interpretation of square-foot-gardening style. Here are my takeaways, that I plan to fix next year.

Zone: 9-B

  1. Tomatoes: 7/10: I started Jubilee Goldens and Better Boys from seed indoors in late January. Transplanted 2 of each in a raised bed in late March. I got a seedling for a 'Glory of Moldova' and planted that in April. Overall, I was happy with the result - great tomatoes, started yielding in June and are still producing delicious tomatoes. What went wrong: I went on extended vacation in June/July, and did not keep up with pinching the suckers - ended up with giant overgrown bushes, instead of nice single-stemmed plants. Next year, I plan to keep them under control better. The other big problem with tomatoes was mice - they got to the tomatoes before I did - I probably lost 40% of my crop to them.

  2. Cherry tomatoes: 5/10: I planted way too many, and too densely because I did not have room. Got a great harvest - red, orange and black - but next year I am going to plant just two of each and thin down to just one. These things grow really crazy, and they smothered their neigboring plants.

  3. Okra - 5/10 - started Clemson Spineless seeds indoors in January and transplanted to raised bed in March. This was way too early, and they plants did NOTHING till July. Next year, I am going to wait till later to start them. The other mistake was to plant only 4 of these. They each produce about 1 pod a week - not enough to do anything with. At this rate, I need 10 plants to give me a useful harvest.

  4. Carrots, Beets, daikon Radishes: 2/10: I had lousy results with root crops in my raised bed. Planted loads of them, most seeds germinated but the seedlings got chewed up by slugs or something. The ones that survived gave generally poor results. I started another batch of seeds in containers, where I hope I can control the pest issues better.

  5. Kale: 8/10: Great plant, the only downside is aphid infestation all through summer. I had to spray with neem almost once a week to keep things under control.

  6. Eggplants: 9/10: Started 'Black-Beauty' seeds indoors in Feb. Transplanted 3 plants out in April. Started yielding in July, and are still going strong. No pest issues to speak of.

  7. Armenian Cucumber: 4/10: I started this late, and did not have an ideal spot to plant it, so my results were not great. Got maybe 2 or 3 of these, over a foot-long cucumbers, very tasty. But the vine wasn't healthy. Next year, I plan to start it earlier and give it a proper spot to grow.

  8. Chinese Ridge Gourd: 5/10: Got seeds from my friend, started a little late and planted it near the armenian cuke. Not an ideal spot, but it grew very well. Still producing gourds, but I am not sure I will grow it again - the taste was bland and not interesting. Pretty yellow flowers, though.

  9. Peppers: 9/10: Grew a lot of these - bell peppers, Thai chili, 'jwala' and 'suraj-mukhi' Indian chili peppers, Padrone pepper. Great yield, what's not to like. I did not grow jalapenos or habaneros, mainly because I don't think anyone in my family would eat those anyway.

  10. Herbs: 9/10: Genovese Basil, Thai Basil, Dill, Parsley, Stevia, Lemongrass, Oregano, Sage. Great to have fresh herbs. Just have to keep on top of them and keep clipping them back when they go to flower.

  11. Greens: 8/10: "Kookaburra" spinach, Gynura Procumbens, Arugula, Southern Broadleaf Mustard. Most of these were interplanted wherever I found room. The Gynura sprawled all over, I plan to control it better next year. Also, the flowers on the Gynura smell beyond awful, so don't let it go to flower :-). Arugula flowers have an interesting 'peanut-butter' flavor. Mustard flowers were deliciously spicy.

  12. Berries: 6/10: I planted Strawberries, Goji berry, Fall-golden Raspberries and Boysenberries. Got a little yield from Boysenberries, but not great. The Raspberries did well - got a decent yield from Aug-Sept. Goji berries did well, great yield from June-Sept - but they have some kind of persistent white mold on their leaves that I have to keep under control. Strawberries are great, I just need to propagate them further for next year.

13: Alliums: 10/10: I simply interplanted spring onions, garlic and some regular onions between my other plants all over. No maintenance, great yield, no complaints.
